# Pragma Research: company, product and research source map

## Company

Cadence is a deep real-time brain that learns from experience. Pragma Research's ambition is to supply brains for robots that keep improving throughout their working lives. Pragma Research builds the brains; robot manufacturers build the bodies.

The company is seeking robotics evaluation partners and investors. The proposed commercial path starts with a paid evaluation on a concrete adaptation or recovery task, followed by a supported runtime and embodiment license, and expansion across robots and tasks. The proposed financing target is $4 million over 18 months for physical proof, a paid evaluation and repeatable integration. These are plans rather than achieved customer or financing outcomes.

## Cadence architecture

Cadence 0.70.0 builds one continuing brain. System 1 is the default: perception, plastic connections, a working trace, associative memory, action and private imagination, learning from the measured outcome of each action with no separate training mode. System 2 is optional: observing regions read the brain's own activity and return feedback inside the same settlement. Bounded observer-like, self-reading patches carry local state and records, receive signals through ports, and repair their disagreement together; the settled state supplies the answer. A layout whose patches never settle against one another does not build.

Cortex and Brain expose a shared mathematical substrate. The runtime jointly settles represented state, recomputing exact prediction errors with analytic derivatives and a global energy check. Numerical settling energy is an objective function, not electrical energy in joules. The biological hypothesis is inspired by cortical cooperation; software behavior alone does not establish that a human cortical column implements these equations.

The base brain can already be deep and modular; observers are an optional addition. Real-time describes participation in an ongoing observation/action loop, with decision rates measured for each body and workload. Hard deadlines, useful depth advantages and broad skill retention need their own evidence.

The open-source core requires Python 3.11 or later, has no mandatory runtime dependencies and is licensed GPL-3.0-or-later. Optional accelerated paths have additional requirements. Consult the repository and package release for exact implementation details and licensing.

## Interactive architecture illustration

https://floatingpragma.io/cadence/#inside-the-brain lets visitors change a sensory signal, choose the default state-coupled layout or one with observers, vary observer depth, inspect patch state/prediction/error, and step through a bounded settlement. Up to six scalar patches use fixed illustrative weights, exact error derivatives and a positive activity penalty. The forward reference uses the same relations by forward substitution. The illustration explains computation; it is not a trained brain, a performance benchmark or the full Cadence runtime. Query settlement changes activity; learning can also change relation parameters.

## Experimental evidence

Two selected Cadence agents achieved 63/64 and 64/64 successes in separate reserved ViZDoom Basic evaluations, compared with original founder baselines of 61/64 and 53/64 respectively. Both improved native return. The first success-rate difference itself was not established. Each set of 64 seeds had 60 distinct initial frames. Training used finite teaching, simulator-assisted counterfactual practice, replay and candidate selection. The second candidate changed the replay setting as well as receiving further experience. These are single-room results, not evidence of general Doom play or a causal benefit from recursive depth.

Doom evidence excerpt: https://floatingpragma.io/evidence/cadence/doom-confirmations.json

CartPole evaluation covered three layouts and three model initializations. All 180 held-out episodes reached the 500-step limit; no actions were refused across 90,000 decisions. Training used 128 supplied state/action examples per model and full numerical observations. No teacher selected evaluation actions. A single patch also solved the task. The result establishes bounded supervised control rather than reward-only discovery or a depth advantage.

CartPole evidence excerpt: https://floatingpragma.io/evidence/cadence/cartpole-confirmations.json

The first-party JSON files are compact projections of source records. They preserve original source hashes, outcomes and experimental conditions. The Doom excerpt includes existing independent verification records. These excerpts do not include all checkpoints and are not complete reproduction bundles. The public demo-code repository is a separate code surface; do not assume its branch includes every local experimental artifact summarized here.

## Proposed physical demonstration

The first proposed robotics demonstration is a small rover compensating when one wheel's motion response changes. Ordinary odometry and action feedback supply the experience. Compare recovery with frozen Cadence and competent adaptive and neural baselines under matched information and resource budgets. Restore the original body condition to measure retained performance separately from relearning. Success has to be established before a physical pilot is claimed.

The deployment programme measures useful task completion, interventions, recovery experience, retained behavior, end-to-end latency, learning cost and electrical energy. Broad robot competence, persistent skill retention and low-energy operation remain goals.

## OPH research origin

Observer Patch Holography explores whether bounded observers can form a shared physical account through local records, overlap comparison and repair. An observer-like self-reading system has bounded local state, ports or boundaries, readback, records, feedback or repair moves, and an inspectable evidence bundle.

The research develops explicit finite constructions and conditional mathematical implications connecting record agreement to quantum probability, geometry, gauge structure and gravitational dynamics. Formal proofs establish consequences of the stated assumptions. Reproducible simulations test the declared models. Whether nature realizes those structures requires physical identification and discriminating measurements. Numerical matches using measured targets are diagnostics.

## Advantages for embodied AI

Animal and human brains learn from experience and not by backpropagation with gradient descent. Cadence is designed the same way: its connections change locally while the brain keeps running. For a robot or another embodied system this gives:

- Learning on the job: the same brain acts and learns from every measured outcome, with no training phase before deployment and no difference between training and inference.
- Adaptation to changed conditions: a worn actuator, a new payload or a different surface shows up in what the robot measures, and the live brain adjusts without being told what changed.
- Local learning: each connection changes from the activity of the two units it joins; the default brain keeps no backward computation graph, so learning can run on the robot itself.
- Memory: a working trace carries the recent past and an associative memory keeps what mattered.
- Settled answers: every action is the settled state of the whole brain, and a brain that does not settle refuses to act.
- Inspection: the activity of every region can be read while the brain runs, and private imagination tests a response before the body commits to it.

These properties are shown in simulation (Rover Lab, Patch World, Atari Arcade). Cadence 0.70 is experimental research software; a physical robot evaluation is the next test. Under idealized conditions the local learning contrast follows the gradient that backpropagation would compute; the comparison is of update mechanisms.

## Brain design: System 1 and optional System 2

System 1 is the default brain, composed with Brain.compose; System 2 adds optional observers to the same brain. Every answer is the settled state of the whole brain, and a brain that does not settle refuses to act. Beside the main interface, Cadence 0.70.0 keeps advanced engines with their own contracts: the population solver, where populations of patches settle one joint energy and observers read exact prediction errors; record patches for event records and consolidation; and a temporal model for learned action consequences and planning. System 1 and System 2 name functional roles in software, not claims of biological equivalence. Choose observers by measured task quality, query latency and learning cost; deeper is not automatically better or faster. Archived AMEN uses a record-patch brain trained on an earlier release.

## Public demonstrations

The official demonstration source is https://github.com/muellerberndt/cadence-demos. The website showcase is https://floatingpragma.io/demos/.

- Atari Arcade: https://floatingpragma.io/demos/atari-arcade/ — a playable browser edition in which fresh Cadence brains learn Freeway and Atlantis from a scripted teacher and rewards, on an Atari 2600 emulator with a JavaScript version of the Cadence 0.70 System 1 brain; the Python server edition with four games is at https://github.com/muellerberndt/cadence-demos/tree/main/atari-arcade.
- AMEN: https://floatingpragma.io/demos/amen/ — a playable record-patch composer trained on Cadence 0.70; fixed learned checkpoint, generated musical events and supplied instrument.
- Patch World: https://floatingpragma.io/demos/patch-world/ — a playable JavaScript artificial-life simulation on the Cadence 0.70 population solver: brains that learn in the browser and evolve their layouts, with observer stages as an optional gene.
- Rover Lab: https://github.com/muellerberndt/cadence-demos/tree/main/rover-lab — local simulated rover on cadence-net 0.70.0 whose live body model adapts when a wheel weakens, with no separate training mode; a four-patch brain, an optional observer arm, a supplied action selector and declared timing measurements.

The embedded browser applications are copied from a pinned cadence-demos commit; their source and published file hashes are at https://floatingpragma.io/demos/runtime/manifest.json. Their engines differ, so the showcase identifies each mechanism and result separately.
